intents.name: ios_update_issue
intents.description: Customer is experiencing problems after installing an iOS or macOS update. Symptoms include slowness, crashes, features breaking, WiFi or Bluetooth issues, or the iOS 11 autocorrect I-question-mark glitch. IMPORTANT: Only use this if the problem is clearly tied to a software update. If battery drain is mentioned WITH an update, use ios_update_issue. If battery drain is mentioned WITHOUT any update, use battery_drain.

intents.name: battery_drain
intents.description: Customer reports that their device battery is draining unusually fast, not charging properly, dying at high percentages, or lasting much shorter than expected. IMPORTANT: If the customer mentions battery drain started after an iOS update, use ios_update_issue instead. If the physical charger cable or adapter is broken or exploded, use device_hardware_issue.

intents.name: device_hardware_issue
intents.description: Customer is having a problem with a physical component of their device — screen cracked or flickering, keyboard broken, camera not focusing, microphone not working, buttons stuck, SIM card not recognised, device randomly restarting, or touchscreen unresponsive. IMPORTANT: The problem must be physical hardware. If the device is slow after an update, use ios_update_issue. If a specific app is causing freezes, use app_issue.

intents.name: app_issue
intents.description: Customer is having a problem with a specific named app — it crashes, freezes, shows wrong content, or a feature inside it is broken. Includes Apple apps (Safari, Mail, Music, iMessage, FaceTime, App Store, Maps, Alarm) and third-party apps (Spotify, Instagram, Snapchat, WhatsApp). IMPORTANT: Do NOT use app_issue if the customer cannot log in due to a forgotten Apple ID password or locked account — use account_access. Do NOT use app_issue if the problem started after an iOS update — use ios_update_issue.

intents.name: account_access
intents.description: Customer cannot access their Apple ID, iCloud, App Store, or iTunes due to a forgotten password, locked account, missing verification code, or two-factor authentication problem. Also includes suspicious login alerts and gift card issues. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use account_access if the customer is having trouble with a specific third-party app login (like Netflix or a game) — use app_issue. Do NOT use account_access if the customer is asking about a purchase — use order_purchase.

intents.name: order_purchase
intents.description: Customer has a question or problem related to buying an Apple product, a pre-order, a delivery, a billing charge, or a refund. Includes iPhone X reservation problems, unexpected App Store charges, and refund requests. IMPORTANT: If the customer received their order but the device is physically broken, use device_hardware_issue. If they cannot access their account to make a purchase, use account_access.

intents.name: general_inquiry
intents.description: Customer is asking a general product question (how-to, feature explanation, compatibility) with no specific problem, or the message is too vague to classify. Use this as a last resort only when none of the other intents clearly fit. IMPORTANT: Do not put hardware complaints, app crashes, or update complaints here just because the message is short or uses informal language. Short informal complaints still belong to their specific intent.

labelling_rules: battery + update in same message → ios_update_issue (update is the cause)
app + update in same message → ios_update_issue
very short or vague message with no specific problem → general_inquiry
when genuinely unsure → pick the problem the customer seems most upset about
app login failure → app_issue if the app is broken; account_access if Apple ID/password is the issue
a thank-you or resolution confirmation is NOT a complaint — do not classify it
why_these_7: Intents defined at granularity where two messages in the same bucket receive meaningfully similar Apple Support replies.
why_keywords_for_sampling: Keywords used only for stratified sampling — not for runtime classification. Runtime classification uses LLM with few-shot examples.
